lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Plan a fair test for plant growth under two light conditions: name IV, DV, three controls and one safety note.

FEEDBACK
Strong answer: Only light differs intentionally; controls listed; safety practical.

WATCH FOR
Changing two variables at once and still calling it fair.

teach_steps.example:
WORKED MODEL
IV: ice cube size (whole vs crushed). DV: time to fully melt. Controls: water volume, start temperature, container type. Repeats: three trials each. Safety: wipe spills.

TRY FIRST
Plan a fair test for plant growth under two light conditions: name IV, DV, three controls and one safety note.

FEEDBACK
Strong answer: Only light differs intentionally; controls listed; safety practical.
teach_steps.explain:
A fair test changes one independent variable, measures a dependent variable and keeps controlled variables the same. Plan equipment, repeats and safety before starting.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner base claims on observation, fair tests and design evidence, rather than guessing from a picture alone. Keep every claim linked to what was seen or measured.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the observations, properties or test steps that carry the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Compare your record with the feedback: did you use the same skill and show your evidence? If a result is uncertain, identify what would have to be observed or tested again. One deliberate, evidence-based revision is more useful than writing a longer answer.
teach_steps.notice: Changing two variables at once and still calling it fair. Correct the claim or method, not just the neatness of the diagram.
